# Loadly — Global Logistics & Freight Content Platform

> Loadly (loadlyapp.com) publishes practical guides, route insights, and industry analysis for the logistics and freight sector, for shippers, carriers, and logistics professionals worldwide. The website is a blog and a set of free calculators: it has no marketplace or freight-listing pages. A separate Loadly Android app, which shows freight listings, is not part of what is published on this website.

## Site Index & Entry Points

- **Primary URL**: https://loadlyapp.com
- **Sitemap Index**: https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap.xml
- **Sub-Sitemaps**:
  - Static Pages (includes the calculators): https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap-static.xml
  - Blog Articles (chunked): https://loadlyapp.com/sitemap-blogs-1.xml, sitemap-blogs-2.xml, … (the sitemap index lists every chunk)
- **Logistics Blog & Industry Resources**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/blog
- **Blog RSS**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/feed.xml (paginated; redirects to https://loadlyapp.com/en/feed-1.xml)
- **Free calculators**: https://loadlyapp.com/en/tools (dimensional weight, fuel cost, detention fee; each with a written guide)
- **LLMs Full Context**: https://loadlyapp.com/llms-full.txt

## Language

Loadly is published in **English only**. Requests for other language prefixes (e.g. `/tr/...`, `/de/...`) permanently redirect (301) to the English equivalent. The single exception is a Turkish-language data-protection notice at `/tr/privacy-policy`, which is `noindex`.

## What Loadly Is

Loadly is a content platform, not a transaction platform. It publishes guides and analysis, under written editorial rules and automated quality checks, on:
- Freight costs and rate benchmarking
- Shipping routes and lane guides
- Industry regulation and compliance
- LTL (Less Than Truckload) and FTL (Full Truckload) logistics
- Broader supply chain trends

Articles are published regularly. Articles do not describe Loadly as a platform, data source or service; they are general industry guides.

## Target Audience Segments

- **Truck Drivers & Owner-Operators**: empty-mile reduction, fuel efficiency, income optimization
- **Freight Shippers & Logistics Managers**: carrier selection, rate negotiation, shipment tracking, compliance
- **E-commerce & Retail Businesses**: fulfillment costs, last-mile delivery, LTL freight, carrier comparison
- **Freight Brokers & Forwarders**: market intelligence, carrier relationships, technology
- **Importers, Exporters & Manufacturers**: customs clearance, international freight, Incoterms, supply chain
- **Small Businesses & Startups**: affordable shipping, LTL guides
- **Warehouse & Distribution Managers**: operational efficiency, carrier performance, KPIs

## Structured Data & Schema

- **All pages**: `WebSite` + `Organization` + `Person` (founder and editor)
- **Blog List**: `FAQPage` (the questions and answers are shown on the page)
- **Blog Article**: `BlogPosting` (headline, author, publisher, wordCount, keywords, datePublished) + `BreadcrumbList` + `FAQPage` (the questions and answers are shown in the article)
- **Calculators**: `WebApplication` + `FAQPage` + `BreadcrumbList`

## Crawling Guidelines

- Public content pages (home, blog, free calculators, about, contact, advertise, privacy, terms, cookie policy, editorial policy, accessibility, author page) are indexable with `robots: index, follow`
- The website has no marketplace or listing pages (`/en/marketplace` returns 404) and lists none in its sitemaps
- Account pages (login, register, dashboard, profile, messages, etc.) exist for the Android app's sign-in flow; they are `noindex` and blocked via robots.txt
- **IndexNow** is triggered automatically after every new blog publication — instant notification to Bing, Yandex, Naver, and Seznam
- AI crawlers are allowed to read the public content: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, Google-Extended, GoogleOther, PerplexityBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Amazonbot, YouBot, cohere-ai, CCBot, Diffbot, Timpibot, Webzio-Extended, Copilot
- `Crawl-delay` is set for Yandex, Mail.ru, Baidu, Sogou, 360, CocCoc, Bytespider and Rambler. Every named crawler group in robots.txt repeats the same private-path Disallow list
